## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Pārāyanānugītigāthāniddesa* (Cnd 22) is an exegetical text belonging to the *Cūḷaniddesa* section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. Titled in English as the *Exposition of the Concluding Verses of the Way to the Beyond*, it comments upon the concluding verses (*anugītigāthā*) of the *Pārāyanavagga* [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records two modern translations across two languages [SuttaCentral].
Curated passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral connect the text to other parts of the Niddesa corpus, including the *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23), the *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), the *Purābhedasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 10), the *Dhotakamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 9), the *Ajitamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 5), the *Kāmasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 1), and the *Guhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 2), as well as the *Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga* (Vb 17) and the *Ñāṇakathā* of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1) [SuttaCentral]. Resembling parallels are also noted in Mnd 3 and Cnd 8 [SuttaCentral].
Automated analysis by DharmaNexus documents extensive Pali-internal text reuse, identifying 5,947 matching passages across 213 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its largest sharing partners are other Niddesa texts—predominantly Cnd 23, Mnd 16, Cnd 8, Mnd 14, Mnd 15, and Mnd 2—alongside the base verse collection *Pārāyanānugītigāthā* (Snp 5.19 / Cnd 4), the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Pārājika 4), and the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus agree on significant shared material with Cnd 23, Mnd 16, Cnd 8, Mnd 2, Mnd 10, and Vb 17 [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali literature, DharmaNexus aligns passages with Sanskrit and Tibetan works, including the *Dharmaskandha*, the *Satyasiddhiśāstra*, the *Patna Dharmapada*, the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, and Chinese texts such as the *Zengyi Ahan jing* (T 125) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
